title: QoS-tiered probe budgeting and autoscaler hedge for stable SLOs
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: During regional capacity shifts and bursty traffic, our aggressive probe fanout and uniform sampling cause noisy health signals that trigger oscillatory autoscaler behavior and cascading circuit-breaker trips. Goal: design and implement a QoS-aware probe budgeting system that reduces probe cost, prioritizes probes for high-QoS customers, and grants the autoscaler a short hedge window (autoscaler-hedge) to absorb transient probe-induced noise without scaling prematurely. The design should integrate with regional failover, circuit breaker hysteresis, and synthetic warmup probes.
acceptance_criteria: Reduced probe-related autoscaler churn by >= 40% in staged canary region under synthetic spike tests
High-QoS customer readiness checks maintain >= 99.9% success within their SLO SLA during noise events
No increase in tail P99 request latency after enabling probe-budgeting in canary clusters
Dashboards surface probe budget consumption and per-tier missed-probe counts
Runbook updated with hedging thresholds and manual override steps
solution_outline: Introduce a central lightweight Probe Budget Manager that issues per-region, per-service monthly/rolling budgets expressed in probe tokens
Attach QoS tier metadata to routes/customers; high-tier routes get reserved probe tokens and elevated sampling probability
Implement hierarchical sampling: synthetic warmup + reserved sampling for high-QoS + opportunistic sampling for best-effort routes
Autoscaler Hedge: delay reactive scale-down decisions for a configurable hedge_window (e.g., 45s) when probe noise or transient readiness flaps are detected
Circuit-breaker tie-in: when probe budget exhaustion approaches, switch best-effort routes to degraded admission instead of triggering circuit-wide breaker trips
Telemetry: emit probe_token_usage, tier_miss_rate, hedge_activation_count; add Grafana panels and an alert when budget burn-rate exceeds threshold
Experiment in canary region with 5% traffic and measure autoscaler scale-up/scale-down cycles, SLO compliance, and request latencies
updates: 2026-02-22: Spike experiment on probe token accounting prototype completed. Prototype counts align with expected sample rates; overhead ~0.8% CPU on proxy
2026-02-27: Design review with SRE and Product. Agreed to reserve 20% of probe budget for high-QoS customers and keep 10% headroom for synthetic warmups
2026-03-01: Implemented Probe Budget Manager MVP and a per-route QoS flag in routing metadata. Integration tests added (unit + e2e mocks).
2026-03-03: Canary rollout scheduled for region eu-west-1 with 5% traffic. Autoscaler Hedge default window set to 45s, configurable via runtime flag.

2026-03-05: Early canary telemetry shows 32% reduction in readiness flaps correlating with probe-sampling changes. Observed one edge case: long-running requests with intermittent KV-cache misses still caused late readiness flips; added follow-up task to track request-shape-based sampling
comments: Priya Shah (2026-02-25): Trade-off note — longer hedge windows reduce thrash but slightly delay capacity release; we've set conservative defaults and will tune post-canary.
Marco Li (SRE, 2026-02-28): Review: prefer 3-tier QoS (platinum/gold/silver) instead of binary high/best-effort; avoids overfitting to a handful of customers.
Daniel Moore (2026-03-02): Implementation note — added a local fallback when Probe Budget Manager is unreachable: proxies fall back to configured sampling rates to avoid blocking health checks.
